statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 31 U.S.C. § 5324 — Structuring transactions to evade reporting requirements?
statutory.answer: No. 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade reporting requirements, but the facts do not show transactions structured to avoid a CTR threshold or an intent to evade reporting.
statutory.label: contradiction
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade reporting requirements. To apply, the facts must show (1) a person acted “for the purpose of evading” Bank Secrecy Act reporting (e.g., CTR reporting under 31 U.S.C. § 5313), and (2) the person structured/assisted in structuring, or caused/attempted to cause a financial institution to fail to file a required report. Here, the listed cash transactions are large single cash deposits (e.g., ~$33k, ~$86k, ~$86k, ~$106k), which are not broken into multiple sub-$10,000 transactions; they are each well above the typical CTR threshold and thus do not evidence “structuring” to avoid reporting. The fact pattern also lacks any indication of intent “for the purpose of evading” reporting (no mention of splitting deposits, using multiple branches/accounts to stay under thresholds, or instructing the bank not to file). Therefore, the conduct described does not fall within 31 U.S.C. § 5324.
